description:
## Goal

Remove the latent-executable channel from activation analysis because it has no producer and can only publish empty collections. Executable existence continues to come from its actual root/product ownership path, not from a dormant second vocabulary.

## Proof at a3a9761d1

Every CallEmission construction initializes `latent_executables` to an empty Vec. Merge and rebuild paths only concatenate those empty vectors. Therefore the publication loop cannot emit an Executable fact, ActivationAnalysis always stores an empty list, and dump/telemetry consumers can only report emptiness.

## Change

- Delete `CallEmission::latent_executables` and `ActivationAnalysis::latent_executables`.
- Delete all empty initializers, merges, rebuild plumbing, and the unreachable publication loop.
- Delete dump, telemetry, and test handling for the field.
- Delete dump helpers orphaned by removal of the empty section.
- Confirm by repository scan that northstar and agent documentation contain no latent_executables field or publication claim; no documentation rewrite is required.

Executable discovery remains owned by exact root/product demand. No compatibility field or adapter remains.

## Signal and checks

- Repository search finds no `latent_executables` or orphaned dump helper.
- Existing root/executable inventory tests prove executable discovery is unchanged.
- Focused activation-analysis, executable-inventory, and JSONL tests pass.
- Full library, CLI, single-threaded fixture matrix, workspace checks, formatting, and strict clippy pass.
- The one initial matrix timeout is the existing `fz-kdt.175` contention tripwire; both changed and parent branches passed the isolated leg, and the complete rerun passed.
title: Delete the always-empty latent-executable channel from activation analysis
